purpose: Full 20-generation run under the planted-feet physics (bone mass, planted feet, friction cap on projection-induced propulsion) and the corrected scored-interval size_report. Supersedes the historical bd41746 slip baseline; it is not directly comparable to it.

platform.machine: AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS with Radeon 780M Graphics, 16 logical CPUs

commands: nice -n 15 env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 EVOLUTION_DEVICES=primary EVOLUTION_CPU_THREADS=6 cargo run --release -q -- headless --population 100000 --seed 38 --generations 20 --duration 60 --checkpoint runs/planted-feet-seed-38.evo
nice -n 15 env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 EVOLUTION_DEVICES=primary EVOLUTION_CPU_THREADS=6 cargo run --release -q --example size_report -- runs/planted-feet-seed-38.evo 50
nice -n 15 env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 EVOLUTION_DEVICES=primary EVOLUTION_CPU_THREADS=6 cargo run --release -q --example first_generation

first_generation.note: Same values as the calm-default baseline recorded in AGENTS.md; the planted-feet physics does not hand random bodies free propulsion.

timing.scope: Headless evaluation calls, including standard and fine perturbed checks. Excludes archive insertion, breeding, saving, and GUI rendering. First call can include pipeline initialization.

top_50.median_convention: size_report selects the upper middle entry for an even sample count.

acceleration_columns_omitted_from_top_50.reason: top-50.csv keeps the same nine columns as 2026-09-26-bone-cap-seed-38/top-50.csv. The current size_report also prints position-derived pos_peak_g, pos_shake_peak_g and the engine value engine_shake_g; position-derived values include position corrections, so they describe visible shaking rather than the engine's head-shake rule.

limitations: One seed at 100k candidates per generation; not a search A/B comparison, a 3M GUI run, or a throughput acceptance test.
CSV values preserve the precision printed by the source logs; top-50 figures are rounded.
Body length is the sum of bone rest lengths, not the body bounding-box span.

Slip is summed horizontal travel of touching nodes over scored replay intervals, divided by absolute terminal replay distance. Post-fall motion and initial recentering are excluded; terrain contact includes slope.

The champion stores 117.3 m but the size_report CPU replay measures 215.6 m. The archive-admission rule only requires the stored score not to exceed the replay; the stored score comes from the evaluation chain, so a replay above the stored score is not an admission failure.

The top-50 mix is bimodal: small 6-node bodies near 1.6 m and 3.4 kg with slip 0.3 to 0.7, and 7-node bodies up to 5.1 m and 24 kg with slip 1.4 to 2.7. The champion is a 4.14 m, 19.14 kg body, so this seed does not show size pressure removed.

The previous seed-38 baseline at bd41746 measured median total bone length 2.23 m and median slip 0.89 m per replay meter; this run at 614e04a measures 2.69 m and 1.34. The two rows use the same size_report convention but different physics, so the comparison is a physics-change signal, not a controlled A/B.
Machine-local compiler and executable paths were removed. The checkpoint runs/planted-feet-seed-38.evo is local and not committed.
The historical rank-21 archive/replay outlier (111.2 m vs 6.4 m) does not appear in this sample; the worst archive/replay gap here is the champion itself, in the replay-above-archive direction.

The release binary was built while the worktree also held uncommitted scheduler, UI and Cargo changes from a concurrent session. None of them touch the physics modules (cpu_engine, physics, shaders, config, storage, evolution), so fitness, size and slip reflect the 614e04a physics.

A separate headless evolution in the other workspace shared the machine from roughly generation 5 of this run. Fitness values are deterministic and unaffected; the logged evaluation_seconds and wall-clock timing include that contention.
revision_scope: Planted feet (5905316), friction cap (8572d32), bone mass, and CPU archive admission on top of the bd41746 baseline.
